text: This is my ER bill. Twelve hundred and eighty-four dollars... for a sprained wrist.
Forty-three percent of Americans have had a medical bill they thought was wrong. Fewer than half ever push back. And the ones who do? More than a third get it cut.
So why not just ask an AI? Because to ask, I'd have to hand over my name, my birthday, my insurance ID... my diagnosis.

Airlock splits the work across a wall. On your laptop, Gemini Nano reads the bill, in only-on-device mode, so it can never quietly fall back to the cloud. Your identity goes into a vault. Only anonymous line items cross, and cloud Gemini audits them against real billing rules, grounded in Google Search.
Watch. Nano reads the photo, right here. Name, member ID, birthday, the hospital... each one becomes a token. The real values stay in an encrypted vault, on this laptop.
And before a single byte leaves, a guard, written in code, not in a prompt, checks it. Hide an ID in a description, and the request is blocked.
It found the X-ray, billed twice. Two hundred and twelve dollars. And it questioned a level-five ER code for a sprained wrist, and told me which rule it's relying on.
The cloud drafts the dispute letter with placeholders. Back on the device, Airlock fills in the real details. The finished letter never leaves your laptop.
Turn the internet off, and the private half still works. Explanations run on-device when they can, and in the cloud when they can't, because they carry no identity.
One SDK. Three inference modes, each one chosen on purpose.
Airlock. Fight the bill... not your privacy.
